Commentary.Commentary: Ireland had to toil hard. They looked tired in the end but have a big task ahead. Ireland have to show their skills with the bat and look for big partnership. It didn't work for them with the ball will hope to showcase their talent with the bat. The Irish bowlers were beaten all apart as every bowler leaked too many runs. It is now time for them to see out this session without losing any wickets. Stay tuned.

Sri Lanka won the toss and it was all about four batters who went onto hit centuries. Initially, Dimuth Karunaratne and Mendis combined to add more than 280 runs and laid a perfect foundation for others to motor along. Sri Lanka lost two wickets quickly on Day 2 but Sadeera Samarawickrama joined Dinesh Chandimal in the middle to add another 183 runs to get near the 600-mark.

Sri Lanka have declared on 591! Dimuth Karunaratne probably was waiting for these two to hit the centuries and they have got it. A humongous score from the Lankan team. They are well ahead in this game and have done an excellent job with the bat.

Hello and welcome to the action of Day 2 between Ireland and Sri Lanka. Day 1 thoroughly belonged to the home team who came up strong with the bat and made it count for a long time. They have relatively two new batsmen in the crease and will hope for a big stand between them. For Ireland, the last session on Day 1 gave some relieve as they struck thrice but have to continue the good work as there is a lot of batting left. The first session will be very important for them as they will look for wickets in quick time. Stay tuned.
...Day 2, Session 1...

Ireland were guilty of bowling far too many boundary balls, they were quite short or very full, their bowlers also offered a lot of width which made scoring very easy for the hosts. The spinners were a tad disappointing as all of them had a economy of over 4. Mark Adair was the pick, he got just the one wicket but managed to keep it tight. Their bowlers though will get some confidence with the way they ended the day but they will need a few more wickets early at the start of Day 2. Sri Lanka on the other hand, will just want to keep batting. The action for the second day begins at 1000 IST (0430 GMT). The build-up though begins a lot earlier. Till then, take care and goodbye!

The day clearly belongs to Lanka but Ireland will be happy with how they have performed in the final session. Yes, they let the Lankans score freely but they have managed to take three wickets. However, the efforts from Dimuth Karunaratne and Kusal Mendis has taken their side well ahead in the game. After Lanka lost one early, the two combined to put up a 200-plus run stand. Both got to tons and laid the platform for a big first innings score.
On the stumps, kept out. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!

Another session which belongs to the Lankans! They did not lose a wicket and have scored freely. Both Dimuth Karunaratne and Kusal Mendis are cashing in on the conditions which are really good to bat on. The partnership between the two is nearing 200. Dimuth Karunaratne got to his ton and Mendis will be wanting to get to his in the next session. MOre of the same is what Lanka would want. The pitch looks flat but Ireland need to get better with the ball. They were too wayward at the start. The spinners were later introduced and got some spin on offer but lacked discipline as they bowled too many short balls. Curtis Campher though showed some intent as he struck but there was nothing apart from that. Ireland will hope they bowl with more discipline and in good areas to get through this Lanka line-up. Stay tuned for the second session.

A dominating performance so far from the home team. They have not put a foot wrong till now apart from the wicket of Nishan Madushka. Sri Lanka chose to bat first and showed their intent straightaway by playing some lovely shots. Nishan Madushka fell after giving a good start but Mendis joined the skipper and kept the run rate close to 5 and bossed the first session.
